articles.title: Scout Troop 14 Announces New Hours for Fall

body: The Bellwood Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
The plan calls for accessible ramp along Union Avenue, with work expected to start in November.
Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings. Public works estimates the work will take about 33 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Parish and Park Groups Team Up on Senior Exercise Class
articles.deck: Residents of Upper Commons filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for senior exercise class along Glen Street, with work expected to start in April. Rosalind Dalrymple, who has lived in Upper Commons for 28 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The Upper Commons Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

articles.title: Block Party Returns to Marsh Landing
articles.deck: Organizers expect about 5 people and say winter coat drive is the main draw.
body: Several residents on Meadow Court said they had been waiting since 1987 for something like this.

The effort began in September when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about winter coat drive. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Bellwood Chapel on Friday at 7 p.m.
The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Foxglove Heights Elementary Teams Head to Winter Tournament
articles.deck: The program begins in March and is open to all students in grade 6 and up.
body: The board will review the results at the end of the winter term. Principal Carl Szabo said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.

Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for March. Students will meet on Friday afternoons in the Hickory Ridge rec center, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

articles.title: Library Adds Seasonal Farmers Market This Fall
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: The event will be held at the Kettle Hill Park gate, rain or shine, with a backup date set for the following Monday.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Letters: Cooper Street Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Cooper Street use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the October meeting.

Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Cooper Street for 21 years, and I want to say what a difference the Bellwood Chapel has made.
Please keep the neighborhood watch sign program in the budget. Many of us on Cooper Street use it every week.
Elias Tanaka, Lower Millrace

articles.title: Gloria Reyes, 84, Carpenter
articles.deck: Friends remember Gloria Reyes for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Mill Hill Lions Club in his or her name.
Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Gloria Reyes spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Council Approves $12,000 for Vernon Street Repairs
articles.deck: The vote came after 30 residents spoke at Tuesday’s session.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 30 weeks once it starts in July.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

Councilmember Sadie Kessler asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $12,000. The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to Scout Troop 14
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.

To the editor: I have lived on Hazel Place for 22 years, and I want to say what a difference Scout Troop 14 has made. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting.
Please keep the pet adoption fair in the budget. Many of us on Hazel Place use it every week.
Vincent Sokolov, Kettle Hill
